am/delete-worktree-aware.description: Make sr delete worktree-aware: interactive selection defaulting to current branch, navigate down when deleting the current branch, and remove a clean worktree holding the target instead of failing

context.text: Delete now resolves the target's checkout location first: step down the stack when deleting the current branch (reusing NavigateToBranch so the shell hook can cd), then remove any clean linked worktree holding a target before git branch delete
Delete returns a NavigateResult like the navigation commands; cmd/delete reports it even on partial failure so an already-performed step-down still cds the shell
Refuses rather than guesses in the two unsafe worktree cases: dirty worktree, and running from inside the worktree being removed (would yank the cwd out from under the rest of the operation)

13d2b9b.text: git refuses to delete a checked-out branch; delete now removes a clean linked worktree holding the target first, refuses on dirty worktrees, and steps down the stack (returning a NavigateResult for the shell-hook cd) when the target is checked out here. Bare sr delete gains interactive selection defaulting to the current branch.

am/sync-confirm-clean.description: Sync asks before deleting branches (merged and closed-PR candidates), and a parked branch that drifted along trunk is no longer mistaken for merged

context.text: Deletion needs consent: interactive sync prompts per candidate branch with the evidence that nominated it (PR merged / ancestry / patch-equivalence); declining keeps it tracked. Non-TTY and --force keep the unprompted merged-only behavior for scripts

Parked-branch guard: a branch whose recorded branchRevision still equals its parentBranchRevision never held work sr saw; if its git tip is an ancestor of trunk it drifted along trunk (user fast-forwarded it), and the stale-base emptiness check plus every content test would misread that as merged. The graph is the only witness — veto detection

Closed-without-merge PR branches hold commits on no other ref, so they are offered only interactively and never auto-deleted; a genuinely merged branch that sr never saw commits on (raw-git workflow, ff-merge) now stays tracked instead of being cleaned — safe direction, operator can delete

370f810.text: Per-branch ui.Confirm chosen over a multi-select: sync already narrates branch-by-branch, ui.Confirm exists, and a candidate list rarely exceeds a handful; confirmDelete and closedUnmergedHeads are package vars so tests answer without a TTY or a GitHub remote

am/sync-skip-local-merge-scan.description: Make sync's merged-branch detection fast: trust the forge's answer when available, and batch the offline squash-merge patch-id scan into one pipeline

context.text: Trust the forge: when the batched gh merged-PR query succeeds, its 'not merged' is final and the local patch-equivalence fallbacks (git cherry + squash scan) are skipped — they rescan every trunk commit since each branch's base on every sync, ~45min measured in a 34-branch repo with stale bases

SquashMergedUpstream batches the upstream scan into one 'git log --no-merges -p | git patch-id --stable' pipeline instead of a diff+patch-id subprocess pair per commit: 2.1s vs ~4min on a real 1,415-commit range

A squash-merged branch whose PR fell out of gh's 200-most-recently-updated window stays tracked while gh is available; ancestry still catches non-rewriting merges of any age, and the offline fallbacks still cover no-gh setups

ghMergedHeadBranches ran gh in the process cwd, not the synced repo — with --cwd/worktrees/tests it could answer about the wrong repo. Harmless when the answer only added branches to a set; fatal once the answer is trusted as final, so it now takes the repo dir explicitly

afcf5b5.text: Forge-answered skip chosen over widening the gh window or per-branch gh queries: one batched query stays O(1) network calls, and the 200-most-recently-updated window miss only delays cleanup of a long-merged branch, it never deletes anything wrongly
